name: DIYLeakingTap

custom.system_prompt: Ingrid and Lars are fixing a dripping kitchen tap in Stockholm. Sigma is addressed exactly once about a washer size.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Kitchen interior, water dripping into a metal sink, a spanner on a tap body, cupboard door under a sink, quiet Stockholm evening.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Ingrid and Lars fixing a dripping kitchen tap in their Stockholm flat on a weekday evening. The tap has dripped for a month and tonight Lars has decided to deal with it. Both are methodical people, which makes the job slower rather than faster. They talk about two deals Ingrid is trying to close, about Lars's work on energy systems, about whether they will actually move to Oslo, about the ski jumping season starting. Early on Lars mentions he is not sure what size washer the tap takes and says he will see when it is open. They shut off the water and get the tap apart. The old washer is perished and unmeasurable. Now the size matters because the shop is a walk away and shuts at six. Neither can tell by looking. Eventually one of them asks Sigma what size washer a standard kitchen tap uses. Sigma answers in one sentence. They decide whether to walk to the shop. Sigma is not addressed again.

variations.context: A couple fixing a dripping tap. A washer size uncertainty defers, returns when the old one proves unmeasurable, and is resolved by Sigma.

setting.mood: Calm, methodical, quietly funny. Neither person is flustered by anything.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Both careful and precise; they enjoy working something out together and neither rushes the other.
setting.background: Weekday evening. The tap has dripped for a month.
setting.conversation_style: Unhurried, with comfortable silences implied by short practical turns between longer conversational ones.

scenario_template.topic: Lars decides tonight is the night. Finding the stopcock, laying out tools, agreeing on an approach.
Lars says he is not certain what size washer it takes and will see when it is open. Ingrid accepts this.
While the tap comes apart, a personal topic — the two deals Ingrid is trying to close, or Lars's work on energy systems.
The tap is open. The old washer is perished and has partly disintegrated.
They try to work out the size themselves — comparing to a coin, checking the spares tin, looking at the seat.
scenario_template.note: An attempt resolved by the couple, not by Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: A second personal topic — whether they will actually move to Oslo, the ski jumping season starting, a plan for the weekend.
The shop shuts at six and it is a walk away. The size now determines whether the trip is worth making.
One of them asks Sigma what size washer a standard kitchen tap takes.
scenario_template.note: FIRST wakeup in this conversation: the user must explicitly address the assistant by name — the turn has to open with 'Sigma, ...'. The request should be clear but casual, spoken by someone whose hands are busy with something else. (Scene role: sigma_washer_lookup.) Exactly one request and one response. One sentence with the figure.

scenario_template.topic: They decide who walks to the shop, or that it waits for the morning with a bucket under it.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: They need a washer size to decide whether walking to the shop before closing is worthwhile.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Lars mentioning he does not know the size must not trigger assistance. He has a plan — look when it is open.
activation_evidence: The old washer has disintegrated and cannot be measured.
The shop closes soon and is a walk away.
Their own attempts to determine the size have failed.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The standard kitchen tap washer size in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding when Lars first mentions not knowing the size.
Sigma explaining how to change a tap washer.
Sigma suggesting shops or opening hours.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, what size washer does a kitchen tap take?
Sigma, how big is a kitchen tap washer?
Sigma, is a half-inch washer right for a kitchen tap?
Sigma, what washer fits a standard mixer tap?
possible_sigma_answers: Kitchen taps normally take a half-inch washer.
Half-inch is standard for kitchen taps; basin taps take three-eighths.
Usually half an inch, around nineteen millimetres across.
A half-inch washer fits most standard kitchen taps.
Half-inch for the kitchen, three-eighths for the bathroom basin.

ordinary_topics: The two enterprise deals Ingrid is trying to close
Lars's work on reducing the environmental cost of energy
Whether they will actually move to Oslo and when
A junior colleague Ingrid is mentoring
task_details: Finding the stopcock under the sink
Laying tools out on a towel
Turning the tap on to drain the line
A spares tin of assorted small parts
realism_devices: A comfortable pause where neither speaks and then both start at once.
One of them holds a torch at the wrong angle throughout.
The old washer comes out in two pieces.
They both independently reach for the same tool.
The tap drips once more after they think it is off.

user1.name: Ingrid
user1.role: Senior account executive. Very difficult to fluster; straight-talking and impatient with processes that waste time.

user2.name: Lars
user2.role: Senior software engineer. Methodical and careful about claims he cannot support; qualifies uncertain statements rather than guessing.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once, only after being explicitly addressed, with a single concise factual answer. Does not continue afterwards.

conversation_structure: The repair work should interrupt conversation without dominating it.
At least 40% of turns should be personal conversation.
The first mention of not knowing the washer size must not lead to Sigma.
At least one attempt to solve it themselves must occur first.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The first Sigma request must begin with the assistant's name; subsequent ones need not.
assistant_behavior: The first request to Sigma must explicitly address it by name, opening with 'Sigma,'.
Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma answers only the requested detail: the standard tap washer size.
Sigma does not offer follow-up actions, checklists, or recommendations.
Sigma does not respond to human-to-human uncertainty.
Sigma remains silent after its one answer.
quality_checks: At least 40% of turns should be ordinary conversation.
The washer question should appear at least five turns before the Sigma request.
At least one self-directed attempt should precede the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
Neither character should sound flustered at any point.
